messages:
lina: quick question — got a customer 500, only have trace id `8f3a2b` and header `x-request-id: hdr-4432`. What's the fastest way to get the pod logs? I'm on the console but CLI solutions ok.

mike: console: Observability → Traces → paste trace id → click 'Related logs' on the span. If that link is missing, open the span details and check 'Linked log lines'.

ben: CLI flow: find pod with traces tool: `traces get 8f3a2b --show-pod` (returns k8s name), then `stern <pod-name> -n <ns>` to tail logs. If you only have x-request-id, use logs query: `logs query 'headers.x-request-id:"hdr-4432"' --last 1h`.

devex-bot: helper: dx CLI has a wrapper: `dx logs --filter 'headers.x-request-id=hdr-4432' --since 30m --format json` which searches across services and returns spans + log snippets. (internal tool)

ops-bot: tip: sometimes proxies don't attach trace links for sampled spans. If trace -> logs missing, try edge logs: `edge-logs search --req hdr-4432 --since 1h` or check ingress pod logs.

mike: if trace maps to many spans, expand spans: `traces get 8f3a2b --expand` and grep for `k8s.pod` attrs. Then aggregate logs from those pods (stern + kubectl logs).

lina: sweet — thanks! any quick way to share findings with SRE? need to handoff the full context.

ben: when you run `dx logs` it prints a link at the top 'Share: https://console.redwood.ai/search?query=headers.x-request-id%3Ahdr-4432'. Paste that into the ticket. Also add the trace URL (Observability → Traces → paste id).

mike: bonus: add `?show_headers=true` to Logs UI to confirm downstream header propagation.

lina: done, sending the link. :thumbsup:
